answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance arises when each identity must hold a distinct computational vertex in a peer-verified reputation graph. An attacker spawning many fakes is forced to bridge unique, costly proofs of original reasoning for every one, much as a raven must gather separate shiny objects. Because generating coherent, non-duplicated responses consumes real inference compute or API credits, the attacker’s expense scales directly with the number of identities, rendering mass Sybil campaigns economically unviable.
